---
title: "Python answer tests"
subtitle: "Basis questions, matrix conditions and your own checker"
---

A question may have many mathematically correct answers. This guide helps you
choose a test for a space or property and shows how ordinary STACK response
trees (PRTs) continue to award the marks. The [worked questions](../examples.qmd)
let you try each choice.

## For teachers

### Choose the mathematical test {#choose-the-mathematical-test}

| Task | Answer test | What counts as correct |
|---|---|---|
| Give this particular matrix | `AlgEquiv` | Corresponding entries are equivalent and dimensions agree. |
| Give any basis of a matrix's null, column or row space | `PythonChecker` with a basis function | Independent vectors span that space, regardless of the particular basis chosen. |
| Give a matrix satisfying stated conditions | `PythonChecker` with a property function | The submitted matrix has the expected properties; each may earn its own marks. |

The basis and matrix-property examples use one
[supplied checker file](../questions/matrix-checkers.py).
`PythonChecker` calls the named function; the usual response trees (PRTs)
still decide marks and feedback. `AlgEquiv` is an existing STACK answer-test
name. `PythonChecker` is an addition to this port, so a native Moodle STACK
version needs equivalent Maxima checks and may need different matrix-input
settings.

### Basis questions: use the matrix in the question {#basis-questions-use-the-matrix-in-the-question}

If the prompt asks for a basis of $\ker A$, the PRT compares the learner's
proposed vectors against the **original matrix $A$**, not against one
precomputed list of basis vectors. Select the `basis` checker with the
`space` option set to `nullspace`; use `columnspace` or `rowspace` for the
other two spaces.
The input's model answer can be generated from $A$ with the matching author
helper. Another independent basis is still correct. For example, if
$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\end{pmatrix}$, both the columns of
$\begin{pmatrix}-2&-3\\1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and those of
$\begin{pmatrix}-5&-1\\1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ span $\ker A$.

| `space` option for `basis` | Space being checked | How learners enter vectors |
|---|---|---|
| `nullspace` | Null space of the original $A$ | One vector per column |
| `columnspace` | Column space of the original $A$ | One vector per column |
| `rowspace` | Row space of the original $A$ | One vector per row |

The [basis examples](../examples.qmd#matrix-problems-from-ingmat-3a)
show alternate correct responses and learner-selected column counts. The
matrix editor cannot represent an empty basis, so choose a task with a
nonzero-dimensional answer space.

After checking a basis, green marks a nonzero vector in the target space when
the valid submitted vectors are independent; it can still belong to an
incomplete family. Yellow marks a dependent valid family and red marks zero
or out-of-space vectors. These colors explain the answer; the PRT awards marks
only for the complete basis in the examples. Edits and resizing clear the
colors.

### Matrix conditions and partial credit {#matrix-conditions-and-partial-credit}

The [determinant-one task](../examples.qmd#find-a-nonidentity-matrix-with-determinant-one)
accepts any integer $2\times2$ matrix with determinant $1$ except the
identity. Three PRTs give one third of the score each: integer entries,
determinant and nonidentity. An entry-by-entry comparison with the model
would reject other correct matrices.

| `property` option for `matrix_property` | Expected result supplied in PRT `tans` | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| `integer_entries` | `true` or `false` | Are all entries integers? |
| `determinant` | An exact rational value such as `1` | Does this square matrix have that determinant? |
| `identity` | `true` or `false` | Is it the identity matrix? |

The PRT's `tans` is the **expected property result**, not the matrix in the
prompt. For determinant one it is `1`; for nonidentity it is `false`.
The supplied file provides one `matrix_property` function with these three
choices. It also has the positive-definiteness functions below. A question
can select any registered function in this file or another author Python file.

### Positive definite matrices {#symmetric-positive-definite-matrices}

A positive definite matrix has a positive quadratic form for every nonzero
vector. The full task also requires Hermitian symmetry, which is ordinary
symmetry for real matrices. The checker uses **Sylvester's criterion** with
exact arithmetic, for both real and complex entries.

You can grade the two conditions together or give separate marks for each.
The independent positivity check uses the real part of the quadratic form.
These four examples show the scoring choices:

| Matrix | Hermitian (symmetric here)? | Positive definite? | Combined / separate marks |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ | Yes | Yes | $1$ / $1$ |
| $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ | No | Yes | $0$ / $1/2$ |
| $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ | Yes | No | $0$ / $1/2$ |
| $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ | No | No | $0$ / $0$ |

Use integers or exact fractions for real and imaginary parts; enter `%i`
for $i$. For example, `matrix([2,%i],[-%i,2])` earns full credit.

The first activity uses `is_hpd` for one overall decision. Its PRT awards
full credit when both conditions hold. See the
[authoring walkthrough](#author-the-spd-checker) for the XML and Quarto block.

```{.stack-question #docs-spd-matrix}
#| label: docs-spd-matrix
#| file: ../questions/symmetric-positive-definite.xml
#| question: A positive definite matrix
#| python-checkers: ../questions/matrix-checkers.py
#| review: true
```

[Download the question XML](../questions/symmetric-positive-definite.xml) ·
[View the checker file](../questions/matrix-checkers.py) ·
[Try it with the other matrix examples](../examples.qmd#symmetric-positive-definite-matrix)

The second activity uses `is_hermitian` and `is_positive_definite` in two
PRTs, each worth half the marks. Each condition has its own feedback.

```{.stack-question #docs-spd-separate}
#| label: docs-spd-separate
#| file: ../questions/symmetric-positive-definite-prt.xml
#| question: Hermitian symmetry and positive definiteness separately
#| python-checkers: ../questions/matrix-checkers.py
#| review: true
```

[Download the two-PRT question XML](../questions/symmetric-positive-definite-prt.xml) ·
[Compare the two authoring patterns](#author-the-spd-checker)

## For developers

### Use the supplied matrix checkers

Save the [supplied checker file](../questions/matrix-checkers.py) with your
question materials. Each matrix PRT uses `PythonChecker`, puts the learner
matrix in `sans`, and selects a function and optional choice in `testoptions`:

| Task | `checker` | `options` object | PRT `tans` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basis of the null, column or row space of `A` | `basis` | `{"space":"nullspace"}`, `{"space":"columnspace"}` or `{"space":"rowspace"}` | The original `A` |
| Integer entries | `matrix_property` | `{"property":"integer_entries"}` | `true` or `false` |
| A particular determinant | `matrix_property` | `{"property":"determinant"}` | An exact value such as `1` |
| Identity matrix | `matrix_property` | `{"property":"identity"}` | `true` or `false` |
| Hermitian symmetry, positivity or both | `is_hermitian`, `is_positive_definite`, `is_hpd` | Omit (defaults to `{}`) | `true` or `false` |

For the null space of an author variable `A`, the input model can use
`<tans>nullspace_basis(A)</tans>` and the PRT node uses the **original** `A`:

```xml
<answertest>PythonChecker</answertest>
<sans>ans</sans>
<tans>A</tans>
<testoptions>{"checker":"basis","options":{"space":"nullspace"}}</testoptions>
```

Use `columnspace_basis(A)` with `{"space":"columnspace"}`, or
`rowspace_basis(A)` with `{"space":"rowspace"}`. For a determinant-one
condition, use the matrix input in `sans`, `<tans>1</tans>`, and
`<testoptions>{"checker":"matrix_property","options":{"property":"determinant"}}</testoptions>`.
Separate PRTs can
award separate marks for integer entries, determinant and nonidentity.
The input's `tans` is a model matrix; a property PRT's `tans` states its
expected result.

The supplied basis and elementary property functions require exact
rational entries (integers or fractions). The positive-definiteness
functions accept exact rational real and imaginary parts. Matrix inputs
have 1–16 rows or columns and at most 64 cells; the [matrix input
guide](matrix-input.qmd) explains learner-selectable dimensions. An empty
basis cannot currently be entered. The build and authored tests exercise
the model answer through the selected checker; choose a model that satisfies
the question and include qtests for alternate correct and wrong responses.
The checker runs on **Check answer**, while **Validate answers** checks
input syntax and settings. The PRT branches, not colored vectors or cells,
award credit.

### Author the positive-definiteness question {#author-the-spd-checker}

The same [matrix checker file](../questions/matrix-checkers.py) registers
`is_hermitian`, `is_positive_definite` and their conjunction `is_hpd`.
It checks the Hermitian part with exact arithmetic. The
[complete one-PRT XML](../questions/symmetric-positive-definite.xml)
uses a $2\times2$ matrix input with model answer
`<tans>matrix([1,0],[0,1])</tans>`. The model sets the input shape;
other correct matrices also earn full credit. Its decision node is:

```xml
<answertest>PythonChecker</answertest>
<sans>ansm</sans>
<tans>true</tans>
<testoptions>{"checker":"is_hpd"}</testoptions>
<truescoremode>=</truescoremode><truescore>1</truescore>
<falsescoremode>=</falsescoremode><falsescore>0</falsescore>
```

The [second XML question](../questions/symmetric-positive-definite-prt.xml)
uses two response trees so each condition earns half the total:

| PRT | Checker | Weight | Awarded when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symmetry` | `is_hermitian` | $0.5$ | $A=A^*$ |
| `positivity` | `is_positive_definite` | $0.5$ | The positivity condition holds |

Each PRT uses `<tans>true</tans>`, scores `1` on its true branch and
`0` on its false branch. Because the two tests are independent, a
non-Hermitian matrix with a positive Hermitian part earns half credit.
For all-or-nothing grading, choose `is_hpd` in one PRT or route a
successful symmetry node to a positivity node. The XML owns scores and
feedback; the checker decides the mathematical condition.

Add the XML and **the checker filename** to a root-level Quarto page:

````markdown
```{.stack-question}
#| label: python-checker-api-a-positive-definite-matrix
#| file: questions/symmetric-positive-definite.xml
#| question: A positive definite matrix
#| python-checkers: questions/matrix-checkers.py
#| review: true
```
````

For the separately weighted question, change `file` to
`questions/symmetric-positive-definite-prt.xml` and `question` to
`Hermitian symmetry and positive definiteness separately`. A page inside
`docs/` uses `../questions/...` paths. Quarto includes the selected
source for browser grading; the XML only names a function. There is no
additional source setting.

Test the authored cases from the project root with the same filename:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$(ls _extensions/ctm-checkers/*.whl | paste -sd: -)  # ctm-checkers' two wheels
python -m ctm_checkers.stack.cli test \
  --file questions/symmetric-positive-definite.xml \
  --python-checkers questions/matrix-checkers.py
python -m ctm_checkers.stack.cli test \
  --file questions/symmetric-positive-definite-prt.xml \
  --python-checkers questions/matrix-checkers.py
quarto render
```

The XML files include alternate real and complex matrices and examples of
each scoring outcome. Try `matrix([2,%i],[-%i,2])` for full credit and
`matrix([1,%i],[%i,1])` in the two-PRT question for the positivity half.
The [live activities](#symmetric-positive-definite-matrices) show both
scoring policies.

### PythonChecker API and a scalar example

Use the supplied matrix functions or write your own `PythonChecker` rule.
Save a Python file beside your question materials, register a named function in
its `CHECKERS` dictionary, then give Quarto that **filename** in
`#| python-checkers:`. Quarto reads the file when it builds the page and
includes its source for browser grading; the XML only names the function.
The [positive-multiple example](../examples.qmd#custom-python-checker) checks any
positive integer multiple of a given number. Its author module contains:

```python
def positive_multiple(student, teacher, options):
    if student.is_Integer is not True:
        return {"valid": False, "correct": False,
                "feedback": "Enter an integer value."}
    return bool(student > 0 and student % teacher == 0)

CHECKERS = {"positive_multiple": positive_multiple}
```

The XML names the checker and passes the learner input and teacher value:

```xml
<answertest>PythonChecker</answertest>
<sans>ans</sans>
<tans>d</tans>
<testoptions>{"checker":"positive_multiple"}</testoptions>
```

Select the module on the Quarto question block as well:

```{.stack-question #docs-custom-multiple}
#| label: docs-custom-multiple
#| file: ../questions/python-checker.xml
#| question: A positive integer multiple (PythonChecker)
#| python-checkers: ../questions/checkers.py
#| variants: 3
#| review: true
```

Both filenames in this block are relative to this `.qmd` page. For the CLI,
filenames are relative to the working directory. There is no separate source
configuration to maintain. `sans` must directly name an input. `tans` can
be a parsed teacher answer or author value, such as the divisor `d`.
`testoptions` is a JSON object. Its required `checker` key names one entry
in `CHECKERS`; its optional `options` key is another JSON object passed to
that function. For example,
`{"checker":"basis","options":{"space":"nullspace"}}` selects `basis`
and passes `{"space":"nullspace"}`. With no `options` key, the function
receives `{}`, as in `{"checker":"positive_multiple"}`. An options
object can hold several named settings, including nested arrays or objects.
For an author-written `my_rule`, for example,
`{"checker":"my_rule","options":{"mode":"strict","weights":[1,2]}}`
passes a Python dictionary with both settings; the function decides what
they mean.
The checker name is a case-sensitive ASCII identifier of at most 64
characters, beginning with a letter and followed by letters, digits or
underscores. Options are JSON values, not CAS or Python expressions; they
are not interpolated with author variables. The selected module is author
code packaged with the page; use only code you trust and expect learners
to be able to see in a published site.

#### Callable and values

Each registered function must be callable with the three positional arguments
`student`, `teacher` and `options`, and finish synchronously. The first two
are parsed values, not raw answer strings: the learner's submitted answer
and whatever teacher value the PRT's `tans` selects. This could be an
expected Boolean for a property question or the original matrix for a basis
question. `options` is the parsed JSON object described above. The API does not
pass a context object or question state. Scalar expressions are SymPy
expressions; matrices are
immutable SymPy matrices. Lists and finite sets are distinct `ListValue` and
`SetValue` objects with ordered `.args` (a set retains its submitted entries).
Equations have two `.args`; held logic has `.operator` and `.operands`;
logical constants use SymPy `true` and `false`. The collection and logic types
and `collection_items` are available from `ctm_checkers.stack.checker_api`.
These values do not promise to retain the learner's exact written arithmetic
form. A custom checker decides its own mathematical domain, within the
existing input and parser limits.

Return a Python `bool` for an ordinary true/false decision, or a dictionary:

```python
{"valid": True, "correct": False, "feedback": "Try another value."}
```

Both required fields must be Python booleans. Use `valid=False` for a response
outside this checker's domain: the learner sees an invalid-input diagnostic
and the PRT's false branch does not run. Use `valid=True, correct=False` for
a mathematically wrong response within the domain. `feedback` is optional
plain text of at most 4,096 characters. A checker cannot return a score or an
answer note; the PRT branches control those. Exceptions and malformed results
are authoring errors, rather than wrong student answers.

For a matrix, a valid result may also include one diagnostic axis:

```python
{"valid": True, "correct": False,
 "assessment": {"columns": ["correct", "dependent"]}}
```

Choose exactly `rows` or `columns`, with one status per submitted vector.
Statuses are `correct`, `incorrect`, or `dependent`. They color the editor but
do not award marks. A checker may omit the assessment entirely. If several
visited PRT nodes supply an assessment for one input, the last one displayed
wins. A quiet PRT node suppresses its checker diagnostic and assessment. The result
cannot include extra keys, an assessment for an invalid response, or a
SymPy Boolean in place of a Python `bool`.

#### Test and publish

Run authored tests with the same module you render:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$(ls _extensions/ctm-checkers/*.whl | paste -sd: -)  # ctm-checkers' two wheels
python -m ctm_checkers.stack.cli test \
  --file questions/python-checker.xml --python-checkers questions/checkers.py
```

The build checks referenced names, function signatures and model-answer
grading on each rendered variant. Add qtests for alternative correct answers, wrong
answers, and important PRT branches. **Validate answers** checks syntax and
input rules; the custom predicate runs on **Check answer**. The page includes
the selected Python source so the same checker runs in local tests and the
learner's browser. Keep secrets out of the module, use available Python and
SymPy features, and avoid local imports or services that the browser cannot
provide. Make checker functions deterministic; do not rely on module state
persisting from one check, variant or test to the next. Custom code can perform
arbitrary computation, so review it before
publishing. The API does not install packages or add new input types. For code
that imports questions directly, `import_xml(xml_path, python_checkers=module_path)`
selects the source; call `ctm_checkers.stack.checkers.preflight(question, variants)`
before publication to run the same author checks. `grade()` and
`run_question_tests()` execute the selected predicate on visited PRT nodes.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Technical limits

A module may register at most 32 named functions in `CHECKERS`. Its source
must be a nonempty UTF-8 file no larger than 64 KiB. Feedback is plain text
up to 4,096 characters. Custom execution does not gain a server process or
additional package installation; apply a process timeout to local test runs
if authored code could take a long time.
:::
